sources.citation: González de Pérez, María Stella. 2016. Presentación. In Ezequiel Uricoechea, Gramática de la lengua chibcha [re-edition of Gramática, vocabulario, catecismo i confesionario de la lengua chibcha, París 1871] (Biblioteca Básica de Cultura Colombiana, Filología). Bogotá: Ministerio de Cultura / Biblioteca Nacional de Colombia. Epub, ISBN 978-958-8959-41-2.
sources.note: Nothing on Duit prosody. The presentation says only: 'Enriquece la introducción con un pequeño texto en lengua duit —posiblemente se habló en Duitama—, único ejemplo conocido hasta hoy sobre dicha lengua, y un corto vocabulario de la lengua sínsiga —variante viva del uwa—, lenguas que nos presenta, acertadamente, como posibles variantes del muisca o, al menos, emparentadas con este.' The one 'acento' hit in the page is Uricoechea's own remark about foreign accent when pronouncing French r, not word stress.

sources.citation: Montes Giraldo, José Joaquín. 1978. Fitónimos de sustrato en el español del altiplano cundiboyacense y dialectos muiscas. Thesaurus: Boletín del Instituto Caro y Cuervo 33(1): 41-54.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone for Duit or Muisca. The only phonological content is segmental and dialectal: 'en el muisca o chibcha del altiplano de Bogotá había.. una partición dialectal entre la zona que tenía como centro a Bogotá.. y la que giraba alrededor de Tunja.; la alternancia ch ~ rr sería uno de los rasgos fónicos que determinaban tal división' (p. 54), with the historical direction argued to be rr > ch.
sources.venue: Thesaurus: Boletín del Instituto Caro y Cuervo

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page duit1239 (refs: Uricoechea 1871 'Catecismo Duit' [text, Glottolog's most extensive description]; Lehmann 1920 Zentral-Amerika [overview;wordlist]; Constenla-Umaña 2012 'Chibchan languages' [overview;comparative]).
sources.note: Bibliographic only; no grammar, sketch or phonology exists for Duit; Glottolog's most extensive description type = text (2 pp., 1871).

sources.citation: Krohn, Haakon S. 2021. Vowel systems of the Chibchan languages / Sistemas vocálicos de las lenguas chibchas. Forma y Función 34(2). doi:10.15446/fyf.v34n2.88423.
sources.note: States in the introduction that 'Stress and tone are not considered to be vowel features, and are thus' outside the paper's scope; Duit is named once in the classification and nowhere else. No prosodic content for any Chibcha-Duit language. File not kept (noted).

sources.citation: Pache, Matthias J. 2018. Contributions to Chibchan historical linguistics. PhD dissertation, Universiteit Leiden. Sec. 2.3.11 'Duit', pp. 355–357; 2.3.11.1.1 'Duit vowels and suprasegmentals', pp. 355–356.
sources.note: Silent on Duit stress: the subsection headed 'Duit vowels and suprasegmentals' only tabulates the five vowel graphemes from Uricoechea and notes possible non-syllabic allophones of i/u; p. 355 states 'The only data on this language are available from Uricoechea's 1871 work'. (For the sister language Muisca, pp. 431–432: 'There are no indications that tone, stress, or vowel nasality were contrastive in Muisca … In Lugo's work, stress is mostly (in approximately 70 to 80% of the cases) indicated on the last syllable of a word', citing Constenla Umaña 1984b: 103–6 — Muisca, not Duit.)

sources.citation: Chevrier, Natacha. 2017. Analyse de la phonologie du bribri (chibcha) dans une perspective typologique. Thèse de doctorat, Université Lyon 2. Annex sec. 1.4 'Muisca et duit : consonne labio-vélaire', p. ~412.
sources.note: Nothing on Duit accent; states Muisca and Duit have not been spoken since the 18th century, descriptions rest on colonial documents and 'aucune donnée phonétique n'est disponible' (regarding the labial-velar).

sources.citation: Gómez Aldana, Diego F. (ed.). 2008-. Muysccubun: diccionario muysca en línea (muysca.cubun.org). Entries gua(2), nga(2), hachua, chihine, pquahaza, ysy, chie(2), z-, bica carry Duit cognates from Uricoechea 1871 tagged '(Gómez)', some with reconstructed IPA bearing stress marks.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No prose statement. Stress marks appear only inside the compilers starred/derived reconstructions, e.g. "*'ɡuwaa (duit) *'ɡuwa (duit)" under gua(2), "ˈkʷaɾe (duit)" under pquahaza, "*ˈuⁿda → ˈoʒ → ˈoɾ (duit)" under ysy. These are wordlist-style marks on hypothesised forms, not a description of Duit accent; treated as wordlist-only data.

sources.note: Read in context (scanned). Only segmental/orthographic remarks: dialect differences between Bogotá and Tunja; suppression of r among the Bogotá Chibcha vs names in -quira in the north; 'se dice que el idioma chibcha carece de las letras l y d.. En cuanto a la segunda [d], es frecuente en el idioma duit o de Tundama, del reino de Tunja'. Nothing on accent, stress or tone.

sources.citation: Uricoechea, Ezequiel. 1871. Gramática, vocabulario, catecismo i confesionario de la lengua chibcha según antiguos manuscritos anónimos e inéditos. (Collection linguistique américaine 1.) Paris: Maisonneuve. Introducción pp. xl–xlii: Duit catechism specimen with Spanish and Muisca parallels and a glossary footnote.
sources.note: Nothing. The sole primary attestation of Duit is a two-page written specimen; a few acute accents appear in the transcription (Tótia 'Hijo', Uequéneca '¿de qué modo?', chí 'ser') without any comment on accent or pronunciation.
